evidence_class: response-open baseline design feasibility only; no future outcome

anchor_rule.ge3: choose observed Thalassia-positive meter marks nearest q25/q50/q75 site_m, requiring unique anchors where possible
anchor_rule.eq2: one anchor at each positive mark plus a third independent lateral/perpendicular-offset core at the midpoint-nearest positive mark
anchor_rule.eq1: three independent non-overlapping offset cores adjacent to the single positive mark

interpretation: Spatially distributed three-core sampling is directly feasible at 30 of 33 recent Thalassia-positive nodes. Only three sparse nodes require a predeclared reduced-spatial-coverage fallback; those nodes retain their design-class label in analysis and reporting.
decision: Use the q25/q50/q75 positive-meter-mark anchor rule for primary TNC sampling where >=3 positive marks exist. Keep sparse-node fallbacks fixed; do not choose core positions from TNC results.
claim_boundary: Recent vegetation state is used only for prospective sampling geometry.
No TNC assay values or future biological outcomes are available or used.
Sparse nodes remain eligible but provide less within-node spatial representation and must retain that design-class label.
Do not relocate cores after assay results are known.
